text:
alex: Hey team — seeing a perf regression on the routing hotpath after the driver bump on dev nodes (535.98 -> 536.12). nsys traces show a lot of kernels mapped to <unknown> and NVTX ranges are missing. Anyone hit CUPTI weirdness?

maria: can you paste the exact nsys command you ran?

alex: sure, here's what I used:
```
nsys profile --output trace.nsys --trace=cuda,nvtx,osrt ./run_batch_test.sh
# result: many <unknown> entries in kernel timeline, KV cache load spikes not attributed
```

sam: we saw something similar on 536.x — CUPTI activity callbacks appeared to not fire for kernels launched via our runtime's stream pool. do you still have CUDA API events?

alex: CUDA API events are present (launches, memcopies), but the activity records for a subset of kernels are unnamed. snippet from timeline:
```
0.000 - 0.012 cuBLASGemm_kernel
0.012 - 0.015 <unknown>
0.015 - 0.022 <unknown>
# NVTX: [batch-start] marker missing around these ranges
```

jordan: i pulled `nvidia-smi -q` on the node — Driver Version: 536.12. dmesg has a few entries too:
```
[ 1234.567890] NVRM: Xid (13): PGRAPH 00000000:...
```

maria: quick try: on one of our CI boxes i forced cupti preload and it recovered names. command i ran:
`LD_PRELOAD=/usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libcupti.so nsys profile --output t2 --trace=cuda,nvtx ./run_batch_test.sh`
that brought kernel names back for most runs.

sam: interesting — LD_PRELOAD helping suggests a symbol/loader ordering issue or CUPTI registration timing. also try `--capture-range=nvtx` + explicit NVTX ranges in the app (torch.cuda.nvtx.range_push). in some setups you need a `cudaDeviceSynchronize()` before stopping capture to flush activity.

alex: LD_PRELOAD improved things but there are still intermittent <unknown> entries on heavy load. doesn't fully eliminate the gap. suspecting a driver/CUPTI regression.

jordan: filing internal ticket PRF-1472 and tagging eng-runtime/support. for mitigation we can either pin nodes back to 535.98 or use the nsys version we validated (nsys 2024.1) on the canary pool. I'll attach dmesg + `nvidia-smi -q` output to the ticket.

profiling-bot: alert: perf-regression-delta +14% p99 on routing hotpath correlated with driver 536.12 rollout (detected by nightly perf job).

maria: also noticed KV cache eviction timeline looked different when kernel names drop — likely because our hotspot identification relies on kernel-level attribution. perfetto captured scheduling slices (timestamps) but not names, so the hotpath latency looked opaque.

sam: action items: (1) collect `dmesg` + full nsys run with `--stats` and attach to PRF-1472, (2) try LD_PRELOAD approach on 2 controlled nodes and document % improvement, (3) run canary with driver pinned to 535.98 and compare p99, (4) try perfetto capture to correlate GPU scheduling vs. missing activity. i'll take (2) and (3).

alex: thanks — i've uploaded a minimal repro script and a short timeline screenshot to the ticket. i'll follow up with the exact NVTX points to reproduce missing ranges. :thumbsup:
